# Android Lab Record — Agent Instructions

> **Read this before making any changes to the lab record document.**

## Project Overview

This project generates a formatted PDF lab record (`Android_Lab_Record.pdf`) for an Android Development course. Each lab entry shows:
- Program number, date, and title
- Full `MainActivity.java` source code
- Full `activity_main.xml` source code
- Output screenshot(s)

## ⚠️ Critical Architecture Note

**`Android_Lab_Record.tex` is auto-generated. Never edit it directly.**

It is produced by `build.py`. Any manual edits will be overwritten the next time `build.py` runs.

---

## File Structure

```
Android_Lab_Record/
├── build.py                    ← THE build script (edit this, not the .tex)
├── Android_Lab_Record.tex      ← Auto-generated by build.py. DO NOT EDIT.
├── Android_Lab_Record.pdf      ← Compiled output
│
├── code/
│   ├── program1/
│   │   ├── MainActivity.java
│   │   └── activity_main.xml
│   ├── program2/ ...
│   └── programN/               ← Source files for each program
│
├── Output_Screenshots/
│   ├── 1.png                   ← Single screenshot (programs with one image)
│   ├── 4_1.png, 4_2.png        ← Multiple screenshots (programs with two images)
│   └── ...
│
└── generated/                  ← Intermediate per-line .tex fragments (by gen_code.py)
                                   Not used in the current build flow. Safe to ignore.
```

---

## How to Add a New Program

### Step 1 — Create the source code files

```
code/programN/MainActivity.java
code/programN/activity_main.xml
```

Where `N` is the program number (e.g. `7` for Program 7).

### Step 2 — Add the output screenshot(s)

Place screenshot(s) in `Output_Screenshots/`:

| Scenario | Filename(s) |
|---|---|
| Single screenshot | `N.png` (e.g. `7.png`) |
| Two screenshots | `N_1.png` and `N_2.png` (e.g. `7_1.png`, `7_2.png`) |

### Step 3 — Register the program in `build.py`

Open [build.py](build.py) and append a new entry to the `PROGRAMS` list (around line 109):

**Single screenshot:**
```python
{
    'number': 7,
    'date': 'DD/MM/YYYY',
    'title': 'Your program title here.',
    'java': 'code/program7/MainActivity.java',
    'xml':  'code/program7/activity_main.xml',
    'output': r'\includegraphics[width=0.45\textwidth]{Output_Screenshots/7.png}',
},
```

**Two screenshots (side by side):**
```python
{
    'number': 7,
    'date': 'DD/MM/YYYY',
    'title': 'Your program title here.',
    'java': 'code/program7/MainActivity.java',
    'xml':  'code/program7/activity_main.xml',
    'output': (r'\includegraphics[width=0.4\textwidth]{Output_Screenshots/7_1.png}'
               r' \quad '
               r'\includegraphics[width=0.4\textwidth]{Output_Screenshots/7_2.png}'),
},
```

### Step 4 — Build and compile

Run from the project root:

```bash
python3 build.py
tectonic --chatter minimal Android_Lab_Record.tex
```

Or as one line:
```bash
python3 build.py && tectonic --chatter minimal Android_Lab_Record.tex
```

> **Note:** `tectonic` automatically downloads missing LaTeX packages on the first run. Subsequent runs are faster.

---

## How the Build Works (Technical Details)

### Why `build.py` instead of writing TeX directly?

LaTeX's `longtable` package tracks page-break state per row. When code is placed inside table cells (as was the original approach), it becomes an unbreakable box — LaTeX either fits the entire chunk on the page or pushes it to the next page, leaving large blank gaps.

**The solution:** Each line of source code becomes its own `longtable` row. This lets LaTeX break between any two consecutive code lines, giving seamless page-to-page flow with zero wasted whitespace.

However, `\input{file}` inside `longtable` breaks this — `longtable` loses its row-tracking state at file boundaries. So `build.py` inlines all rows directly into the `.tex` file at build time.

### Character escaping

`build.py` escapes these LaTeX special characters in source code:

| Source char | LaTeX output |
|---|---|
| `\` | `\textbackslash{}` |
| `{` `}` | `\{` `\}` |
| `#` `$` `%` `&` | `\#` `\$` `\%` `\&` |
| `^` `~` | `\^{}` `\textasciitilde{}` |
| `_` | `\_` |
| `<` `>` | `\textless{}` `\textgreater{}` |
| ` ` (space) | `\ ` (explicit TeX space, prevents collapsing) |
| `\t` (tab) | `\ \ \ \ ` (4 spaces) |

### Line spacing

Controlled by `\arraystretch` in `TABLE_HEAD` (line 76 of `build.py`):

| Value | Effect |
|---|---|
| `1.0` | Tightest — native font line height |
| `1.1` | **Current default** — recommended for code |
| `1.5` | Original (too spacious) |

Change this value and rebuild if you need tighter or looser spacing.

---

## Common Issues

### Long lines overflow the column
A line of code is wider than `0.94\textwidth`. Fix by breaking it manually in the source file, or add `\sloppy` handling in `build.py`'s `code_rows()` function.

### Screenshot is missing
`tectonic` will fail with a "file not found" error. Make sure the screenshot file exists in `Output_Screenshots/` with the exact filename specified in the `output` field of `PROGRAMS`.

### Program appears in wrong order
The `PROGRAMS` list in `build.py` is ordered. Programs are rendered in list order, each starting on a new page. Keep the list sorted by program number.

### Special characters look wrong in PDF
Check the escaping table above. If a character produces wrong output, add a new entry to the `ESCAPES` dict in `build.py`.
